koreanEslErrorPairs.error: Congo is very poor because resource curse happened by bad luck.
koreanEslErrorPairs.correction: According to Source C, Congo's poverty is not caused by an inevitable resource curse, but by the cynical decisions of corporate actors.
koreanEslErrorPairs.explanation: Korean learners often treat the 'resource curse' as an accepted natural law. In Source C, the author explicitly argues that 'there is no curse; rather, corporate actors are to blame.'

koreanEslErrorPairs.error: King Leopold owned the Congo and then independence made everything free.
koreanEslErrorPairs.correction: Although the DRC achieved independence 64 years ago, historical lands were never returned to Congolese owners and remain controlled by foreign private equity.
koreanEslErrorPairs.explanation: Do not assume political independence resolved property rights. Emphasize the continuity of foreign corporate land ownership.

koreanEslErrorPairs.error: Police fired bullets so people are sad because plantation.
koreanEslErrorPairs.correction: When residents in Lokutu demonstrated against harsh plantation conditions in March 2019, company-directed police fired live ammunition into the crowd.
koreanEslErrorPairs.explanation: Replace childish, fragmented phrasing with precise historical details (Lokutu, March 2019) and formal cause-and-effect transitions.

koreanEslErrorPairs.error: U.S. fund funnels profits to investors and laborers get no money.
koreanEslErrorPairs.correction: A U.S.-based private equity fund controls commercial plantations, funnelling profits to elite investors while local labourers are subjected to unpaid wages.
koreanEslErrorPairs.explanation: Use advanced participial modifiers ('funnelling profits') and academic passive voice ('are subjected to') to elevate sentence sophistication.

finalWritingSupport.g1Scaffold: Provide a fill-in-the-blank chronological template focusing on three clear dates: 1884 (King Leopold), 2019 (Lokutu), and present day (tech extraction and rejection of the curse). Pre-teach 'are subjected to' and 'rather... to blame'.
finalWritingSupport.g2Extension: Prompt students to analyze the rhetoric of economic euphemism: compare how global economists use 'resource curse' to obscure responsibility, whereas Mousseau uses 'corporate actors' and 'land grabs' to demand legal and moral accountability.
teacherCorrectionPriorities: Ensure students do not exceed 140 words or fall below 100 words.
Check that the student includes explicit attribution ('According to Source C').
Verify that at least three specific historical/modern details are cited (Leopold/Berlin, private equity/Lokutu, tech/palm oil).
Confirm that the student explains the rejection of the 'resource curse' accurately.
Ensure no outside political facts or graphic inventions are introduced.

detailedReadingGuide.sourceLayoutNote: Source C is presented as a three-paragraph historical/current-affairs article with a source header ('Source C:') and bibliographic citation ('Soleil-Chandi Mousseau, African Arguments, ‘Colonialism Revamped in the Democratic Republic of the Congo’, 2024'). Below is the granular 15-sentence analysis providing deep linguistic and pedagogical scaffolding for Grade 9 ESL learners.

sentenceAnalysis.original: 140 years ago this November at the Berlin Conference, Belgium’s King Leopold was recognized as the sole owner of the Congo Free State, a territory including the entirety of today’s Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).
sentenceAnalysis.chunkReading: 140 years ago this November / at the Berlin Conference, / Belgium’s King Leopold / was recognized as the sole owner / of the Congo Free State, / a territory including the entirety / of today’s Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).
sentenceAnalysis.directKorean: 이번 11월로 140년 전 / 베를린 회담에서, / 벨기에의 레오폴드 국왕은 / 유일한 소유자로 인정받았습니다 / 콩고 자유국의, / 전체를 포함하는 영토인 / 오늘날의 콩고민주공화국(DRC)의.
sentenceAnalysis.naturalKorean: 이번 11월로 140년 전 베를린 회담에서 벨기에의 레오폴드 국왕은 오늘날 콩고민주공화국(DRC) 전체를 포함하는 영토인 콩고 자유국의 유일한 소유자로 공인되었습니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: passive voice structure establishing diplomatic and legal authority granted by foreign powers
mustKnowChunks.example: The sovereign territory was recognized as an independent republic by neighboring nations.

mustKnowChunks.use: noun phrase denoting absolute personal ownership rather than collective state control
mustKnowChunks.example: The investor became the sole owner of the historic shipping company.

mustKnowChunks.use: prepositional participial modifier denoting complete geographical inclusion
mustKnowChunks.example: The national park expanded, including the entirety of the ancient coastal wetland.

sentenceAnalysis.mustKnowGrammar: Introductory prepositional time and place adverbials ('140 years ago this November at the Berlin Conference'); passive matrix clause ('Belgium's King Leopold was recognized as the sole owner'); appositive noun phrase modifying 'the Congo Free State' ('a territory including the entirety of today’s Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC)').
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanation: Imagine if one man walked into an international meeting, / and all the powerful countries agreed / that an entire huge country belonged completely to him, / like his own personal backyard. / That is what happened to the Congo in 1884.
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanationKo: 한 사람이 국제 회의장에 걸어 들어갔는데, / 모든 강대국들이 거대한 나라 전체가 / 마치 그의 개인 뒷마당인 양 온전히 그의 것이라고 합의해 주었다고 상상해 보세요. / 1884년 콩고에 일어났던 일이 바로 그것이었습니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Notice the opening time marker: '140 years ago this November at the Berlin Conference.'
teachingTranscript.korean: 도입부의 시간 표시어구를 보세요: '이번 11월로 140년 전 베를린 회담에서.'

teachingTranscript.english: Point out the passive voice: Leopold 'was recognized as the sole owner.' Foreign powers made this decision without any Congolese consent.
teachingTranscript.korean: 수동태에 주목하세요: 레오폴드는 '유일한 소유자로 인정받았다.' 외세 강대국들이 콩고 주민들의 어떠한 동의도 없이 이 결정을 내린 것입니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Check: What was the territory called in 1884? The Congo Free State.
teachingTranscript.korean: 확인: 1884년에 그 영토는 무엇이라 불렸나요? 콩고 자유국입니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Correction: Do not write that Belgium as a nation owned the Congo in 1884; the text specifies King Leopold personally was recognized as the sole owner.
teachingTranscript.korean: 교정: 1884년에 벨기에라는 국가가 콩고를 소유했다고 쓰지 마세요. 본문은 레오폴드 국왕 개인이 유일한 소유자로 인정받았다고 명시합니다.

sentenceAnalysis.original: Leopold's reign was marked by slavery, millions of deaths, and widespread atrocities committed during the first colonial exploitation of the territory’s exceptional wealth of natural resources.
sentenceAnalysis.chunkReading: Leopold's reign / was marked by slavery, / millions of deaths, / and widespread atrocities / committed during the first colonial exploitation / of the territory’s exceptional wealth / of natural resources.
sentenceAnalysis.directKorean: 레오폴드의 통치는 / 노예제에 의해 특징지어졌습니다, / 수백만 명의 죽음, / 그리고 광범위한 잔혹 행위들에 의해 / 최초의 식민지적 수탈 동안 자행된 / 그 영토의 예외적인 부에 대한 / 천연자원의.
sentenceAnalysis.naturalKorean: 레오폴드의 통치는 그 영토가 지닌 독보적인 천연자원에 대한 최초의 식민지적 수탈 과정에서 자행된 노예제, 수백만 명의 죽음, 그리고 광범위한 잔혹 행위로 얼룩졌습니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: passive idiom indicating prominent defining features or historical hardships
mustKnowChunks.example: The decade was marked by severe drought and widespread agricultural decline.

mustKnowChunks.use: noun phrase describing massive, systemic violations of human dignity
mustKnowChunks.example: International human rights bodies condemned the widespread atrocities committed against civilians.

mustKnowChunks.use: evaluative noun phrase emphasizing immense geological and biological riches
mustKnowChunks.example: The mountain province attracted multinational investments due to its exceptional wealth of natural resources.

sentenceAnalysis.mustKnowGrammar: Passive matrix clause ('Leopold's reign was marked by...'); parallel compound prepositional complements ('slavery, millions of deaths, and widespread atrocities'); past participial phrase modifying 'atrocities' ('committed during the first colonial exploitation of the territory's exceptional wealth of natural resources').
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanation: Because the land had so much rubber and minerals, / King Leopold used forced labor and extreme violence to take it all. / Millions of people died, / making his rule one of the darkest times in history.
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanationKo: 그 땅에 엄청난 양의 고무와 광물이 있었기 때문에, / 레오폴드 국왕은 그것을 모조리 빼앗기 위해 강제 노동과 극단적인 폭력을 휘둘렀습니다. / 수백만 명의 사람이 목숨을 잃었고, / 그의 통치는 역사상 가장 어두운 시기 중 하나가 되었습니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Notice the three parallel nouns following 'marked by': slavery, millions of deaths, and widespread atrocities.
teachingTranscript.korean: 'marked by' 뒤에 이어지는 세 개의 병렬 명사에 주목하세요: 노예제, 수백만 명의 죽음, 광범위한 잔혹 행위입니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Observe how the participial phrase 'committed during...' directly links extreme violence to the economic desire for natural resources.
teachingTranscript.korean: 'committed during...'이라는 분사 구문이 극단적 폭력과 천연자원에 대한 경제적 탐욕을 어떻게 직접 연결하는지 관찰해 보세요.

teachingTranscript.english: Check: What was the primary motivation behind Leopold's atrocities? The colonial exploitation of exceptional natural wealth.
teachingTranscript.korean: 확인: 레오폴드의 잔혹 행위 뒤에 있던 주요 동기는 무엇이었나요? 독보적인 천연자원에 대한 식민지적 수탈이었습니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Correction: Avoid vague terms like 'bad things'; use the author's precise vocabulary: slavery, millions of deaths, and atrocities.
teachingTranscript.korean: 교정: '나쁜 일들' 같은 모호한 표현을 피하고, 작가의 정확한 어휘인 노예제, 수백만 명의 사망, 잔혹 행위를 사용하세요.

sentenceAnalysis.original: 64 years after its independence, the DRC remains plagued by various forms of colonialism and extraction, resulting in massive human suffering, land grabs, human rights abuses, hunger and poverty.
sentenceAnalysis.chunkReading: 64 years after its independence, / the DRC remains plagued / by various forms of colonialism and extraction, / resulting in massive human suffering, / land grabs, / human rights abuses, / hunger and poverty.
sentenceAnalysis.directKorean: 독립 후 64년이 지난 지금도, / DRC는 여전히 괴롭힘을 당하고 있습니다 / 다양한 형태의 식민주의와 수탈에 의해, / 막대한 인간의 고통을 초래하면서, / 토지 약탈, / 인권 침해, / 굶주림과 빈곤을.
sentenceAnalysis.naturalKorean: 독립을 맞이한 지 64년이 흐른 지금도, DRC는 다양한 형태의 식민주의와 자원 수탈로 시달리고 있으며, 이는 막대한 인간의 고통과 토지 약탈, 인권 침해, 굶주림과 빈곤으로 이어지고 있습니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: linking verb + participial adjective construction denoting persistent affliction
mustKnowChunks.example: The coastal community remains plagued by contaminated drinking water.

mustKnowChunks.use: present participial connective phrase introducing tangible consequences
mustKnowChunks.example: The sudden factory closure resulted in massive unemployment across the district.

mustKnowChunks.use: compound noun referring to large-scale, often coercive acquisition of communal land
mustKnowChunks.example: Rural farming families organized protests against illegal corporate land grabs.

sentenceAnalysis.mustKnowGrammar: Introductory prepositional temporal phrase ('64 years after its independence'); copular clause with participial complement ('the DRC remains plagued by...'); present participial clause of result ('resulting in massive human suffering, land grabs, human rights abuses, hunger and poverty').
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanation: Even though Congo got its independence 64 years ago, / the stealing of land and resources never actually stopped. / New groups just found new ways to do it, / leaving regular people hungry and poor.
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanationKo: 비록 콩고가 64년 전에 독립을 얻었지만, / 토지와 자원을 빼앗기는 일은 결코 멈추지 않았습니다. / 새로운 집단들이 새로운 방식으로 수탈을 이어갔고, / 평범한 사람들은 여전히 굶주림과 빈곤에 허덕이고 있습니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Notice the time comparison: 140 years ago Leopold seized it, and 64 years after independence the country is still afflicted.
teachingTranscript.korean: 시간적 비교를 보세요: 140년 전 레오폴드가 영토를 장악했고, 독립 후 64년이 지난 지금도 국가는 여전히 고통받고 있습니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Highlight 'resulting in'—this participial structure packs five severe consequences into a compact academic clause.
teachingTranscript.korean: 'resulting in'을 강조하세요. 이 분사 구문은 다섯 가지 심각한 결과를 간결하고 학술적인 절로 압축해 줍니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Check: Did independence solve the problems of extraction? No, the DRC remains plagued by various forms of colonialism.
teachingTranscript.korean: 확인: 독립이 자원 수탈의 문제를 해결했나요? 아닙니다, DRC는 여전히 다양한 형태의 식민주의에 시달리고 있습니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Correction: Ensure students don't write that colonialism ended in 1960; the author explicitly argues it 'remains plagued by various forms of colonialism'.
teachingTranscript.korean: 교정: 1960년에 식민주의가 끝났다고 쓰지 않도록 주의시키세요. 작가는 여전히 '다양한 형태의 식민주의에 시달리고 있다'고 명시합니다.

sentenceAnalysis.original: Remarkably, the land that became the private property of a Belgian king 140 years ago has still not been returned to its Congolese owners.
sentenceAnalysis.chunkReading: Remarkably, / the land that became the private property / of a Belgian king 140 years ago / has still not been returned / to its Congolese owners.
sentenceAnalysis.directKorean: 놀랍게도, / 사유 재산이 되었던 그 땅은 / 140년 전 벨기에 국왕의 / 여전히 반환되지 않았습니다 / 그것의 콩고인 소유자들에게.
sentenceAnalysis.naturalKorean: 놀랍게도, 140년 전 벨기에 국왕의 사유 재산이 되었던 그 땅은 여전히 원래의 콩고인 주인들에게 반환되지 않았습니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: sentence adverbial expressing analytical surprise or irony at an unresolved injustice
mustKnowChunks.example: Remarkably, the lost historical manuscript survived centuries of war undamaged.

mustKnowChunks.use: noun phrase denoting exclusive individual ownership
mustKnowChunks.example: The entire beachfront was declared the private property of the resort developer.

mustKnowChunks.chunk: has still not been returned to
mustKnowChunks.use: present perfect passive construction emphasizing ongoing failure of restitution
mustKnowChunks.example: The stolen cultural artifacts have still not been returned to their country of origin.

sentenceAnalysis.mustKnowGrammar: Sentence adverb ('Remarkably'); relative clause defining 'the land' ('that became the private property of a Belgian king 140 years ago'); present perfect passive verb phrase ('has still not been returned to its Congolese owners').
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanation: Think about this: / a king stole a massive piece of land 140 years ago. / The country is independent now, / but the people who live there still do not own their land. / It was never given back.
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanationKo: 이것을 생각해 보세요: / 140년 전에 한 국왕이 거대한 땅을 훔쳤습니다. / 그 나라는 이제 독립했지만, / 그곳에 사는 주민들은 여전히 자기 땅을 소유하지 못하고 있습니다. / 결코 반환되지 않은 것입니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Why does the author start with the adverb 'Remarkably'? It highlights the shocking injustice that 140 years later, land restitution never happened.
teachingTranscript.korean: 작가는 왜 부사 'Remarkably(놀랍게도)'로 문장을 시작할까요? 140년이 흐른 뒤에도 토지 반환이 결코 이루어지지 않았다는 충격적인 부당함을 강조하기 위해서입니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Notice the present perfect passive: 'has still not been returned.' The historical injustice remains an active present reality.
teachingTranscript.korean: 현재완료 수동태에 주목하세요: 'has still not been returned.' 과거의 부당함이 현재까지 지속되는 생생한 현실임을 보여줍니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Check: Who legally owned the land 140 years ago according to the text? A Belgian king as private property.
teachingTranscript.korean: 확인: 본문에 따르면 140년 전에 그 땅을 법적으로 소유했던 사람은 누구인가요? 사유 재산으로 소유했던 벨기에 국왕입니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Correction: Do not omit 'Congolese owners'; emphasizing who the rightful owners are is central to the author's argument.
teachingTranscript.korean: 교정: 'Congolese owners'를 생략하지 마세요. 정당한 주인이 누구인지 강조하는 것이 작가 논증의 핵심입니다.

sentenceAnalysis.original: Instead, it is now controlled by a U.S.-based private equity fund, funnelling profits to its high profile investors.
sentenceAnalysis.chunkReading: Instead, / it is now controlled / by a U.S.-based private equity fund, / funnelling profits / to its high profile investors.
sentenceAnalysis.directKorean: 대신에, / 그것은 이제 통제되고 있습니다 / 미국에 본사를 둔 사모펀드에 의해, / 수익을 빼돌리면서 / 유명 투자자들에게.
sentenceAnalysis.naturalKorean: 대신에, 그 땅은 이제 미국에 본사를 둔 사모펀드의 지배를 받고 있으며, 이 펀드는 막대한 이익을 유력 투자자들에게 빼돌리고 있습니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: transitional adverb presenting a stark and unjust alternative to expected land restitution
mustKnowChunks.example: Instead of rebuilding the local clinic, municipal funds were diverted to luxury developments.

mustKnowChunks.use: financial noun phrase denoting an investment partnership that buys and manages companies to generate high returns
mustKnowChunks.example: The global timber operations were bought out by an overseas private equity fund.

mustKnowChunks.use: present participial phrase denoting systematic diversion of wealth to external actors
mustKnowChunks.example: The offshore conglomerate was criticized for funnelling profits to tax-haven accounts.

sentenceAnalysis.mustKnowGrammar: Contrastive sentence adverb ('Instead'); passive matrix clause ('it is now controlled by a U.S.-based private equity fund'); non-finite present participial clause of accompanying result ('funnelling profits to its high profile investors').
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanation: So where did the land go? / It did not go to the people. / Instead, an American investment company bought it, / sending all the money made from the crops / directly to rich foreign investors.
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanationKo: 그렇다면 그 땅은 어디로 갔을까요? / 주민들에게 돌아가지 않았습니다. / 대신 미국의 한 투자회사가 그것을 사들였고, / 작물 재배로 번 모든 돈을 / 부유한 외국인 투자자들에게 곧장 보내고 있습니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Look at the word 'Instead'—it marks the sharp pivot from what should have happened (land returned) to what actually happened (private equity control).
teachingTranscript.korean: 'Instead'라는 단어를 보세요. 마땅히 일어났어야 할 일(토지 반환)에서 실제로 일어난 일(사모펀드 지배)로의 날카로운 전환을 나타냅니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Notice the verb 'funnelling'—it metaphorically conveys how wealth is drained out of the local economy like liquid through a funnel.
teachingTranscript.korean: 'funnelling(깔때기로 쏟아붓듯 빼돌리는)'이라는 동사에 주목하세요. 부가 깔때기를 통해 빠져나가듯 지역 경제에서 유출되는 모습을 비유적으로 전달합니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Check: Who receives the profits from the land today? High profile investors of a U.S.-based private equity fund.
teachingTranscript.korean: 확인: 오늘날 그 땅에서 나오는 이익은 누가 가져가나요? 미국 사모펀드의 유력 투자자들입니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Correction: Teach students that 'private equity fund' is a financial institution, not a charitable foundation.
teachingTranscript.korean: 교정: 'private equity fund(사모펀드)'는 자선 단체가 아니라 영리 금융 투자 기관임을 명확히 지도하세요.

sentenceAnalysis.original: Community members who work as labourers on the plantations are subjected to unpaid wages and harsh working conditions.
sentenceAnalysis.chunkReading: Community members / who work as labourers on the plantations / are subjected to / unpaid wages / and harsh working conditions.
sentenceAnalysis.directKorean: 지역 사회 주민들은 / 농원에서 인부로 일하는 / 당하고 있습니다 / 미지급 임금 / 그리고 가혹한 노동 조건을.
sentenceAnalysis.naturalKorean: 플랜테이션 농원에서 노동자로 일하는 지역 주민들은 임금 체불과 열악하고 혹독한 노동 조건에 시달리고 있습니다.

mustKnowChunks.chunk: work as labourers on the plantations
mustKnowChunks.use: descriptive occupational phrase identifying agricultural field workers
mustKnowChunks.example: Generations of families continued to work as labourers on the coastal sugar plantations.

mustKnowChunks.use: passive phrasal verb denoting subjection to unfair or abusive treatment without power to resist
mustKnowChunks.example: Migrant factory workers were subjected to excessive overtime and dangerous machinery.

mustKnowChunks.use: noun phrase denoting labor performed without financial compensation
mustKnowChunks.example: The union organized a formal strike to demand the immediate recovery of unpaid wages.

sentenceAnalysis.mustKnowGrammar: Complex subject with restrictive relative clause ('Community members who work as labourers on the plantations'); passive verb phrase ('are subjected to'); compound noun phrase objects of preposition ('unpaid wages and harsh working conditions').
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanation: The local villagers do the heavy, dangerous farming work on the plantations. / But the company often does not even pay them their money, / and forces them to work under terrible conditions.
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanationKo: 지역 마을 주민들이 플랜테이션에서 힘들고 위험한 농사일을 합니다. / 하지만 회사는 그들에게 마땅한 급여조차 주지 않는 경우가 허다하며, / 끔찍한 환경 속에서 일하도록 강요합니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Notice the key passive structure: 'are subjected to.' It emphasizes that workers do not choose these conditions; the corporate system forces it upon them.
teachingTranscript.korean: 핵심 수동태 구문인 'are subjected to'에 주목하세요. 노동자들이 이러한 조건을 선택한 것이 아니라, 기업 시스템이 이를 강요하고 있음을 강조합니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Observe the phrase 'unpaid wages.' The workers are literally denied the earnings they worked hard to produce.
teachingTranscript.korean: 'unpaid wages(체불 임금)'라는 표현을 관찰하세요. 노동자들은 열심히 일해 일군 소득조차 정당하게 받지 못하고 있는 것입니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Check: What two abuses do plantation labourers face in this sentence? Unpaid wages and harsh working conditions.
teachingTranscript.korean: 확인: 이 문장에서 플랜테이션 노동자들이 겪는 두 가지 학대는 무엇인가요? 임금 체불과 열악한 노동 조건입니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Correction: Point out that 'labourer' uses British/international English spelling with 'ou'.
teachingTranscript.korean: 교정: 'labourer'가 영국/국제 표준 영어 스펠링(ou)을 사용하고 있음을 짚어주세요.

sentenceAnalysis.original: Their day-to-day life is plagued by violence and repression prosecuted by plantation security forces and police forces directed by the company, with a myriad of unlawful detentions, beatings, torture, and even murders.
sentenceAnalysis.chunkReading: Their day-to-day life / is plagued by violence and repression / prosecuted by plantation security forces / and police forces directed by the company, / with a myriad of unlawful detentions, / beatings, / torture, / and even murders.
sentenceAnalysis.directKorean: 그들의 일상적인 삶은 / 폭력과 탄압에 시달리고 있습니다 / 플랜테이션 보안대에 의해 자행되는 / 그리고 회사에 의해 지휘받는 경찰력에 의해, / 무수한 불법 구금들과 함께, / 구타, / 고문, / 그리고 심지어 살인들까지.
sentenceAnalysis.naturalKorean: 그들의 일상생활은 플랜테이션 보안대와 회사의 지시를 받는 경찰 병력에 의해 자행되는 폭력과 탄압으로 얼룩져 있으며, 무수한 불법 구금과 구타, 고문, 심지어 살인까지 벌어지고 있습니다.

mustKnowChunks.chunk: is plagued by violence and repression
mustKnowChunks.use: passive voice phrase depicting constant, systemic civilian intimidation
mustKnowChunks.example: The border town is plagued by gang violence and military repression.

mustKnowChunks.meaning: 회사의 지휘를 받는, 회사의 지시를 따른
mustKnowChunks.use: past participial modifier showing corporate command over public police units
mustKnowChunks.example: The private guard units directed by the mining company barred journalists from entering.

mustKnowChunks.use: quantifying phrase emphasizing an overwhelming number of abuses
mustKnowChunks.example: The report detailed a myriad of environmental violations across the river basin.

sentenceAnalysis.mustKnowGrammar: Matrix clause in passive voice ('Their day-to-day life is plagued by violence and repression'); two coordinating participial phrases modifying 'repression' ('prosecuted by plantation security forces' and 'directed by the company'); prepositional phrase with compound catalog of nouns ('with a myriad of unlawful detentions, beatings, torture, and even murders').
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanation: Daily life is terrifying for these workers. / Private guards and company-controlled police beat them, / lock them in jail without laws, / hurt them, and sometimes even kill them to keep them quiet.
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanationKo: 이 노동자들에게 일상생활은 공포 그 자체입니다. / 사설 경비대와 회사의 지휘를 받는 경찰이 그들을 구타하고, / 법적 절차 없이 감옥에 가두며, / 고문하고, 때로는 저항을 막기 위해 살해하기까지 합니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Notice the heavy phrase: 'police forces directed by the company.' That shows public law enforcement has been captured by private corporate interests.
teachingTranscript.korean: 묵직한 표현인 'police forces directed by the company(회사에 의해 지휘받는 경찰력)'에 주목하세요. 공권력이 사적 기업의 이익에 종속되었음을 보여줍니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Study the escalating list of nouns at the end: detentions, beatings, torture, and even murders.
teachingTranscript.korean: 문장 끝에 나열된 점층적 명사 목록을 살펴보세요: 구금, 구타, 고문, 그리고 심지어 살인입니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Check: Who carries out the repression? Both plantation security forces and company-directed police forces.
teachingTranscript.korean: 확인: 누가 탄압을 집행하나요? 플랜테이션 보안대와 회사의 지휘를 받는 경찰 병력 둘 다입니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Correction: Teach students that 'myriad' means a vast, countless number.
teachingTranscript.korean: 교정: 'myriad'가 '무수히 많은 수'를 뜻하는 고급 어휘임을 지도하세요.

sentenceAnalysis.original: Residents in Lokutu rose up in March 2019 when the Congolese police, who had been sent to end the demonstrations, ended up firing live bullets into the crowd.
sentenceAnalysis.chunkReading: Residents in Lokutu rose up / in March 2019 / when the Congolese police, / who had been sent to end the demonstrations, / ended up firing live bullets / into the crowd.
sentenceAnalysis.directKorean: 로쿠투의 주민들은 봉기했습니다 / 2019년 3월에 / 콩고 경찰이, / 시위를 종식시키기 위해 파견되었던, / 결국 실탄을 발사했을 때 / 군중 속으로.
sentenceAnalysis.naturalKorean: 2019년 3월, 시위를 진압하기 위해 파견되었던 콩고 경찰이 결국 군중을 향해 실탄을 발사하자 로쿠투의 주민들은 거세게 봉기했습니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: phrasal verb denoting collective civilian rebellion against oppressive injustice
mustKnowChunks.example: Displaced villagers rose up against the corrupt regional authorities.

mustKnowChunks.use: passive past perfect relative clause denoting official mandate to suppress protest
mustKnowChunks.example: Federal troops were sent to end the student demonstrations outside the ministry.

mustKnowChunks.chunk: firing live bullets into the crowd
mustKnowChunks.use: gerund phrase describing lethal force used against unarmed civilians
mustKnowChunks.example: International tribunals denounced security agents for firing live bullets into the crowd.

sentenceAnalysis.mustKnowGrammar: Main clause with past simple verb ('Residents in Lokutu rose up in March 2019'); temporal adverbial clause introduced by 'when'; non-restrictive past perfect passive relative clause modifying 'the Congolese police' ('who had been sent to end the demonstrations'); phrasal verb + gerund construction ('ended up firing live bullets into the crowd').
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanation: In March 2019, the local people in Lokutu protested because they could not take the abuse anymore. / But instead of listening, / the police fired real, deadly bullets into the crowd of protestors.
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanationKo: 2019년 3월, 로쿠투 지역 주민들은 학대를 더 이상 견딜 수 없어 시위를 벌였습니다. / 하지만 그들의 목소리를 듣는 대신, / 경찰은 시위 군중을 향해 치명적인 실탄을 쏘아댔습니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Notice the specific anchor: 'March 2019' and 'Lokutu.' This gives students a concrete, dated case study of corporate resistance.
teachingTranscript.korean: 구체적인 사건 닻인 '2019년 3월'과 '로쿠투'에 주목하세요. 학생들에게 기업 횡포에 저항한 구체적인 연대기적 사례를 제공합니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Look at the phrase 'ended up firing live bullets.' 'Ended up' highlights a tragic, lethal outcome of state repression.
teachingTranscript.korean: 'ended up firing live bullets(결국 실탄을 발사했다)'라는 구문을 보세요. 'ended up'은 국가 탄압이 낳은 비극적이고 치명적인 결말을 부각합니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Check: What happened in Lokutu in March 2019? Residents demonstrated and police fired live bullets into the crowd.
teachingTranscript.korean: 확인: 2019년 3월 로쿠투에서 무슨 일이 있었나요? 주민들이 시위를 벌였고 경찰이 군중을 향해 실탄을 발사했습니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Correction: Ensure students don't confuse Lokutu with a political party; it is a specific geographic location in the DRC.
teachingTranscript.korean: 교정: 학생들이 로쿠투를 정당 이름으로 혼동하지 않도록 콩고민주공화국의 구체적 지역명임을 확인시켜 주세요.

sentenceAnalysis.original: In addition to this historical colonial exploitation, DRC continues to face new forms of extraction, with even more dire consequences for the Congolese people.
sentenceAnalysis.chunkReading: In addition to this historical colonial exploitation, / DRC continues to face / new forms of extraction, / with even more dire consequences / for the Congolese people.
sentenceAnalysis.directKorean: 이러한 역사적 식민지 수탈에 더하여, / DRC는 계속해서 직면하고 있습니다 / 새로운 형태의 자원 수탈에, / 훨씬 더 끔찍한 결과들과 함께 / 콩고 사람들에게.
sentenceAnalysis.naturalKorean: 이러한 역사적인 식민지 수탈에 더하여, DRC는 콩고 주민들에게 한층 더 끔찍한 결과를 초래하는 새로운 형태의 자원 수탈에 끊임없이 직면하고 있습니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: prepositional phrase establishing additive thematic transition between paragraphs
mustKnowChunks.example: In addition to high inflation, the country faced severe energy shortages.

mustKnowChunks.use: noun phrase denoting contemporary corporate and technological resource removal
mustKnowChunks.example: Environmentalists warned that deep-sea mining represents dangerous new forms of extraction.

mustKnowChunks.use: collocation emphasizing severe, catastrophic human impact
mustKnowChunks.example: The prolonged drought had dire consequences for food production across the continent.

sentenceAnalysis.mustKnowGrammar: Introductory additive prepositional phrase ('In addition to this historical colonial exploitation'); matrix clause with continuous infinitive complement ('DRC continues to face new forms of extraction'); prepositional phrase with comparative degree adjective ('with even more dire consequences for the Congolese people').
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanation: The old colonial suffering was bad enough, / but today there are brand new ways people take Congo's riches. / And these new ways bring even worse suffering to regular families.
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanationKo: 과거의 식민지적 고통만으로도 끔찍했지만, / 오늘날에는 콩고의 부를 빼앗아 가는 완전히 새로운 방식들이 존재합니다. / 그리고 이러한 새로운 방식들은 평범한 가정에 훨씬 더 혹독한 고통을 안겨주고 있습니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Notice the transition in Sentence 9: 'In addition to...' bridges Paragraph 2's agricultural plantations to Paragraph 3's broader resource extraction.
teachingTranscript.korean: 9번 문장의 전환에 주목하세요: 'In addition to...'는 2문단의 농업 플랜테이션과 3문단의 더 넓은 자원 수탈을 연결하는 가교 역할을 합니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Look at the adjective 'dire'—it means urgent, terrible, and catastrophic.
teachingTranscript.korean: 'dire'라는 형용사를 보세요. 대단히 끔찍하고 파국적인 상황을 뜻합니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Check: Does the author say new forms of extraction are better or worse than before? They bring 'even more dire consequences.'
teachingTranscript.korean: 확인: 작가는 새로운 형태의 수탈이 이전보다 낫다고 하나요, 더 나쁘다고 하나요? '훨씬 더 끔찍한 결과(even more dire consequences)'를 가져온다고 말합니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Correction: Teach students that 'consequences' here carries an exclusively negative meaning.
teachingTranscript.korean: 교정: 여기서 'consequences'가 전적으로 부정적인 결과를 나타냄을 지도하세요.

sentenceAnalysis.original: For the past three decades, the country has faced bloody conflicts, which have claimed millions of lives, particularly affecting the mineral-rich eastern region of the country.
sentenceAnalysis.chunkReading: For the past three decades, / the country has faced bloody conflicts, / which have claimed millions of lives, / particularly affecting / the mineral-rich eastern region of the country.
sentenceAnalysis.directKorean: 지난 30년 동안, / 그 나라는 유혈 분쟁에 직면해 왔습니다, / 그것은 수백만 명의 목숨을 앗아갔습니다, / 특히 영향을 미치면서 / 그 나라의 광물이 풍부한 동부 지역에.
sentenceAnalysis.naturalKorean: 지난 30년 동안 이 나라는 수백만 명의 목숨을 앗아간 유혈 분쟁에 직면해 왔으며, 이는 광물이 풍부한 동부 지역에 특히 극심한 영향을 미쳤습니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: temporal duration phrase spanning roughly the 1990s through the 2020s
mustKnowChunks.example: For the past three decades, local activists campaigned for indigenous land rights.

mustKnowChunks.chunk: bloody conflicts, which have claimed millions of lives
mustKnowChunks.meaning: 수백만 명의 목숨을 앗아간 유혈 분쟁
mustKnowChunks.use: complex descriptive phrase denoting devastating protracted warfare
mustKnowChunks.example: The civil war resulted in bloody conflicts, which have claimed millions of lives across the region.

mustKnowChunks.use: geographical phrase identifying the epicenter of resource-driven armed competition
mustKnowChunks.example: Militias fought aggressively to control the mineral-rich eastern region.

sentenceAnalysis.mustKnowGrammar: Prepositional temporal duration phrase ('For the past three decades'); present perfect matrix clause ('the country has faced bloody conflicts'); non-restrictive relative clause with present perfect verb ('which have claimed millions of lives'); present participial phrase with focusing adverb ('particularly affecting the mineral-rich eastern region of the country').
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanation: For thirty long years, / wars have raged across Congo, / killing millions of innocent people. / Most of this violence happens in the eastern part of the country / where all the valuable minerals are buried.
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanationKo: 30년이라는 긴 세월 동안 / 콩고 전역에서 전쟁이 벌어져 / 수백만 명의 무고한 사람들이 목숨을 잃었습니다. / 이 폭력의 대부분은 값비싼 광물들이 묻혀 있는 / 동부 지역에서 집중적으로 발생합니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Notice the timeframe: 'the past three decades.' That spans from the 1990s right up to the 2020s.
teachingTranscript.korean: 시간적 범위를 보세요: '지난 30년 동안(the past three decades).' 이는 1990년대부터 2020년대 현재까지 이어지는 기간입니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Connect the geography to geology: why the 'eastern region'? Because that region is specifically 'mineral-rich.'
teachingTranscript.korean: 지리와 지질학을 연결해 보세요: 왜 '동부 지역'일까요? 그 지역이 유독 '광물이 풍부한(mineral-rich)' 곳이기 때문입니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Check: How many lives have these conflicts claimed? Millions of lives.
teachingTranscript.korean: 확인: 이 분쟁들로 얼마나 많은 사람이 목숨을 잃었나요? 수백만 명의 목숨입니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Correction: Ensure students don't guess outside death tolls; cite 'millions of lives' exactly as stated in the text.
teachingTranscript.korean: 교정: 외부의 사망자 통계를 임의로 가져오지 말고 본문에 적힌 '수백만 명의 목숨(millions of lives)'을 그대로 인용하도록 지도하세요.

sentenceAnalysis.original: Violence is not the only consequence of the current forms of exploitation and extraction in the country.
sentenceAnalysis.chunkReading: Violence is not the only consequence / of the current forms of exploitation and extraction / in the country.
sentenceAnalysis.directKorean: 폭력이 유일한 결과는 아닙니다 / 현재 형태의 수탈과 채굴의 / 그 나라에서.
sentenceAnalysis.naturalKorean: 현재 콩고에서 벌어지는 수탈과 자원 채굴이 낳은 결과가 비단 폭력뿐만은 아닙니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: negative rhetorical limiter used to expand inquiry beyond physical warfare into economic damage
mustKnowChunks.example: Physical displacement is not the only consequence of rapid deforestation.

mustKnowChunks.chunk: current forms of exploitation and extraction
mustKnowChunks.use: compound noun phrase referencing contemporary commercial arrangements
mustKnowChunks.example: Scholars analyzed the current forms of exploitation and extraction dominating oceanic fisheries.

sentenceAnalysis.mustKnowGrammar: Inverted negative thematic transition clause; linking verb 'is'; predicate noun phrase 'not the only consequence'; prepositional post-modifiers ('of the current forms of exploitation and extraction in the country').
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanation: War and fighting are terrible, / but they are not the only damage done. / The way companies take the resources / also completely ruins the country’s economy.
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanationKo: 전쟁과 무력 충돌도 끔찍하지만, / 그것만이 유일한 피해는 아닙니다. / 기업들이 자원을 빼앗아 가는 방식은 / 그 나라의 경제 전반을 완전히 파탄에 이르게 합니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Notice the rhetorical function of Sentence 11: it bridges physical violence (Sentence 10) to broader macroeconomic destruction (Sentence 12).
teachingTranscript.korean: 11번 문장의 수사적 기능을 보세요: 물리적 폭력(10번 문장)에서 더 넓은 거시경제적 파탄(12번 문장)으로 시야를 넓혀줍니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Point out how the author pairs 'exploitation' with 'extraction' to reinforce the predatory nature of resource removal.
teachingTranscript.korean: 작가가 'exploitation(착취)'과 'extraction(수탈/채굴)'을 나란히 짝지어 자원 탈취의 약탈적 성격을 어떻게 강화하는지 짚어주세요.

teachingTranscript.english: Check: What other consequence is coming next? Economic impact.
teachingTranscript.korean: 확인: 폭력 외에 다음 문장에서 언급될 또 다른 결과는 무엇인가요? 경제적 영향입니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Correction: Teach students to use 'not only... but also' logic to connect physical and economic consequences.
teachingTranscript.korean: 교정: 학생들이 'not only... but also' 논리를 활용해 물리적 결과와 경제적 결과를 입체적으로 연결하도록 유도하세요.

sentenceAnalysis.original: Whether it is from the firms producing palm oil or from the tech companies profiting from mineral extraction, the exploitation of the DRC’s resources has had a dire impact on the country’s economy.
sentenceAnalysis.chunkReading: Whether it is from the firms producing palm oil / or from the tech companies profiting from mineral extraction, / the exploitation of the DRC’s resources / has had a dire impact / on the country’s economy.
sentenceAnalysis.directKorean: 야자유를 생산하는 기업들로부터이든 / 광물 채굴로부터 이익을 얻는 기술 기업들로부터이든 간에, / DRC 자원의 수탈은 / 대단히 끔찍한 영향을 미쳐 왔습니다 / 그 나라의 경제에.
sentenceAnalysis.naturalKorean: 야자유를 생산하는 기업들 때문이든 광물 채굴로 막대한 이익을 챙기는 기술 기업들 때문이든 간에, DRC의 자원에 대한 수탈은 국가 경제에 대단히 끔찍한 타격을 가해 왔습니다.

mustKnowChunks.chunk: Whether it is from... or from...
mustKnowChunks.use: correlative concessive clause encompassing multiple corporate sectors
mustKnowChunks.example: Whether it is from domestic factories or from foreign importers, pollution must be regulated.

mustKnowChunks.use: noun phrase referencing commercial agribusiness plantations
mustKnowChunks.example: Multinational firms producing palm oil faced consumer boycotts over deforestation.

mustKnowChunks.chunk: tech companies profiting from mineral extraction
mustKnowChunks.meaning: 광물 채굴로부터 이익을 얻는 기술 기업들
mustKnowChunks.use: noun phrase directly linking consumer electronics and tech firms to Congolese mines
mustKnowChunks.example: Global tech companies profiting from mineral extraction face strict supply-chain disclosure laws.

mustKnowChunks.chunk: has had a dire impact on
mustKnowChunks.use: present perfect idiomatic expression denoting severe cumulative harm
mustKnowChunks.example: The prolonged currency collapse has had a dire impact on family savings.

sentenceAnalysis.mustKnowGrammar: Correlative concessive conditional clause ('Whether it is from... or from...'); present participial modifiers ('producing palm oil', 'profiting from mineral extraction'); matrix subject with prepositional phrase ('the exploitation of the DRC’s resources'); present perfect verb with direct object and prepositional phrase ('has had a dire impact on the country’s economy').
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanation: Think about palm oil in your food / and precious minerals inside your smartphone. / Huge companies make billions of dollars from these products, / but the people of Congo see none of that money— / their economy stays ruined.
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanationKo: 여러분이 먹는 음식 속 야자유와 / 스마트폰 속에 들어가는 귀한 광물들을 떠올려 보세요. / 거대 기업들은 이 제품들로 수십억 달러를 벌어들이지만, / 콩고 주민들은 그 돈을 구경조차 하지 못하며 / 국가 경제는 여전히 파탄 난 상태로 남아 있습니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Notice the two industries Mousseau names: agribusiness (palm oil firms) and the modern digital economy (tech companies).
teachingTranscript.korean: 무소 작가가 지목한 두 가지 산업에 주목하세요: 농업 비즈니스(야자유 기업들)와 현대 디지털 경제(기술 기업들)입니다.

teachingTranscript.english: This shows that extraction is not just historical rubber; it is today's smartphones, laptops, and consumer commodities.
teachingTranscript.korean: 이는 자원 수탈이 과거의 고무에만 머무는 것이 아니라, 오늘날의 스마트폰, 노트북, 일상 소비재와 직접 연결되어 있음을 보여줍니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Check: What two corporate sectors are named? Palm oil producers and tech companies profiting from mineral extraction.
teachingTranscript.korean: 확인: 본문에 명시된 두 기업 부문은 무엇인가요? 야자유 생산 기업들과 광물 채굴로 이익을 얻는 기술 기업들입니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Correction: Help students connect 'tech companies' to minerals like cobalt and coltan mentioned in wider discussions, but keep student summaries anchored in the text.
teachingTranscript.korean: 교정: 학생들이 '기술 기업'을 광물 수탈과 자연스럽게 연결하되, 글을 쓸 때는 본문의 어휘를 충실히 따르도록 지도하세요.

sentenceAnalysis.original: Poverty and hunger are widespread through what has often been labelled as the “resource curse,” to describe countries not benefiting economically from their own natural resources.
sentenceAnalysis.chunkReading: Poverty and hunger are widespread / through what has often been labelled / as the “resource curse,” / to describe countries / not benefiting economically / from their own natural resources.
sentenceAnalysis.directKorean: 빈곤과 굶주림은 널리 퍼져 있습니다 / 자주 명명되어 온 것을 통하여 / '자원의 저주'라고, / 국가들을 설명하기 위하여 / 경제적으로 혜택을 받지 못하는 / 그들 자신의 천연자원으로부터.
sentenceAnalysis.naturalKorean: 자신들이 가진 천연자원으로부터 경제적 혜택을 누리지 못하는 국가들을 묘사하기 위해 흔히 '자원의 저주'라고 일컬어지는 현상을 통해 빈곤과 굶주림은 광범위하게 퍼져 있습니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: compound subject with copular predicate describing severe societal destitution
mustKnowChunks.example: Following the economic sanctions, poverty and hunger were widespread across the rural interior.

mustKnowChunks.use: passive participial phrase referencing an economic concept
mustKnowChunks.example: The petro-state's inflation crisis was labelled as the classic resource curse by financial analysts.

mustKnowChunks.use: negative participial clause defining the resource curse paradox
mustKnowChunks.example: Local fishermen found themselves not benefiting economically from the newly opened coastal shipping lanes.

sentenceAnalysis.mustKnowGrammar: Compound subject clause ('Poverty and hunger are widespread'); prepositional phrase containing nominal relative clause ('through what has often been labelled as the “resource curse”'); infinitive clause of purpose/definition ('to describe countries not benefiting economically from their own natural resources') featuring negative present participial modification ('not benefiting economically').
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanation: People often use a special name for this: / the 'resource curse.' / It is an economic idea used to describe countries / that have tons of natural treasure, / but whose citizens are still starving and poor.
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanationKo: 사람들은 흔히 여기에 특별한 이름을 붙입니다: / 바로 '자원의 저주'입니다. / 엄청난 양의 천연 보물을 품고 있지만, / 국민들은 여전히 굶주리고 가난한 나라들을 / 설명하기 위해 쓰이는 경제학적 개념입니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Notice how Mousseau introduces the concept: 'what has often been labelled as the resource curse.' The word 'labelled' hints that this is a convenient tag.
teachingTranscript.korean: 무소 작가가 이 개념을 어떻게 도입하는지 보세요: '자원의 저주라고 자주 명명되어 온 것.' 'labelled(명명된)'라는 표현은 이것이 하나의 편리한 꼬리표일 뿐이라는 암시를 줍니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Look at the definition given in the sentence: 'countries not benefiting economically from their own natural resources.'
teachingTranscript.korean: 문장에 제시된 정의를 살펴보세요: '자신들의 천연자원으로부터 경제적 혜택을 누리지 못하는 국가들'입니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Check: What does the term 'resource curse' describe? Countries that do not benefit economically from their own natural resources.
teachingTranscript.korean: 확인: '자원의 저주'라는 용어는 무엇을 설명하나요? 자신들의 천연자원으로부터 경제적 혜택을 얻지 못하는 국가들입니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Correction: Make sure students notice the quotation marks around “resource curse”—it signals that the author is quoting an external label.
teachingTranscript.korean: 교정: “resource curse”에 붙은 큰따옴표를 학생들이 눈여겨보게 하세요. 작가가 외부의 명칭을 인용하고 있음을 나타내는 신호입니다.

sentenceAnalysis.original: However, looking at the forces driving this exploitation, there is no curse.
sentenceAnalysis.chunkReading: However, / looking at the forces driving this exploitation, / there is no curse.
sentenceAnalysis.directKorean: 그러나, / 이러한 수탈을 이끄는 힘들을 바라볼 때, / 저주란 없습니다.
sentenceAnalysis.naturalKorean: 그러나 이러한 수탈을 추동하는 실질적인 힘들을 들여다보면, 저주 따위는 존재하지 않습니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: vital contrastive transition rejecting conventional economic assumptions
mustKnowChunks.example: The market seemed stable; however, deeper inspection revealed mounting systemic vulnerabilities.

mustKnowChunks.chunk: looking at the forces driving this exploitation
mustKnowChunks.meaning: 이러한 수탈을 이끄는(추동하는) 힘들을 바라볼 때
mustKnowChunks.use: participial viewpoint phrase focusing on institutional and human mechanisms
mustKnowChunks.example: Looking at the forces driving this deforestation, commercial ranching is clearly the primary factor.

mustKnowChunks.use: existential negative clause representing the author's decisive thesis statement
mustKnowChunks.example: Social scientists demonstrated that there is no curse, only policy failure and elite corruption.

sentenceAnalysis.mustKnowGrammar: Adversative sentence connector ('However'); introductory present participial phrase ('looking at the forces driving this exploitation') with restrictive participial post-modifier ('driving this exploitation'); existential clause with negative polarity ('there is no curse').
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanation: Here is the big turning point of the article: / the author says stop calling it a 'curse'! / A curse sounds like magic or bad luck. / But bad luck is not causing this— / real human greed is causing it.
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanationKo: 여기가 바로 이 기사의 가장 결정적인 전환점입니다: / 작가는 이것을 '저주'라고 부르지 말라고 일갈합니다! / 저주라고 하면 마법이나 불운처럼 들립니다. / 하지만 불운이 이를 초래한 것이 아닙니다— / 실재하는 인간의 탐욕이 이것을 초래한 것입니다.

teachingTranscript.english: This is the thesis climax: 'However, looking at the forces driving this exploitation, there is no curse.'
teachingTranscript.korean: 이것이 바로 논제의 절정입니다: '그러나 이러한 수탈을 이끄는 힘들을 바라볼 때, 저주란 없습니다.'

teachingTranscript.english: Notice the rhetorical power of the short, four-word clause: 'there is no curse.' It completely shatters the fatalistic economic myth.
teachingTranscript.korean: 'there is no curse(저주란 없다)'라는 네 단어로 이루어진 짧은 절의 수사적 힘에 주목하세요. 숙명론적인 경제학적 신화를 산산이 깨부숩니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Check: Does the author believe the DRC is suffering from an actual curse? No, the author explicitly states 'there is no curse.'
teachingTranscript.korean: 확인: 작가는 DRC가 실제 저주에 시달리고 있다고 믿나요? 아닙니다, 작가는 '저주란 없다'고 단호하게 명시합니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Correction: Emphasize this strongly: students must not write that Source C confirms the resource curse; Source C refutes it!
teachingTranscript.korean: 교정: 이를 아주 강력하게 강조하세요: 학생들은 Source C가 자원의 저주를 긍정한다고 써서는 절대 안 되며, 오히려 그것을 반박하고 있음을 명확히 써야 합니다!

sentenceAnalysis.original: Rather, it is the cold and cynical attitude of governments and corporate actors that are to blame
sentenceAnalysis.chunkReading: Rather, / it is the cold and cynical attitude / of governments and corporate actors / that are to blame
sentenceAnalysis.directKorean: 오히려, / 냉혹하고 냉소적인 태도입니다 / 정부들과 기업 행위자들의 / 비난받아야 할 것은
sentenceAnalysis.naturalKorean: 오히려 비난받아야 마땅한 것은 바로 정부들과 기업 행위자들의 냉혹하고 냉소적인 태도입니다

mustKnowChunks.use: corrective adverb presenting the true cause after rejecting the false label
mustKnowChunks.example: The disaster was not natural; rather, it was gross municipal negligence that caused the bridge collapse.

mustKnowChunks.use: evaluative noun phrase condemning profit-motivated indifference to human suffering
mustKnowChunks.example: The investigators condemned the cold and cynical attitude of pharmaceutical executives.

mustKnowChunks.use: compound noun phrase identifying the specific entities bearing moral and legal responsibility
mustKnowChunks.example: Both sovereign governments and corporate actors share responsibility for reducing carbon emissions.

mustKnowChunks.use: idiomatic passive-infinitive construction assigning direct culpability
mustKnowChunks.example: Faulty wiring and ignored safety warnings are to blame for the warehouse fire.

sentenceAnalysis.mustKnowGrammar: Adversative corrective sentence adverb ('Rather'); cleft focus construction ('it is the cold and cynical attitude of governments and corporate actors that are to blame'); idiomatic semi-passive infinitive assigning responsibility ('are to blame'). Notice that the original source text ends without a closing period.
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanation: So who is really responsible? / The author points right at the leaders of governments and greedy multinational corporations. / Their cold, uncaring choices to take profit over human lives / are what should really be blamed.
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanationKo: 그렇다면 진짜 책임은 누구에게 있을까요? / 작가는 정부의 지도자들과 탐욕스러운 다국적 기업들을 정면으로 지목합니다. / 사람의 목숨보다 이익을 우선시한 그들의 냉혹하고 무심한 선택이야말로 / 진정으로 비난받아야 마땅한 원인이라는 것입니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Notice the cleft sentence structure: 'it is [X] that are to blame.' It places total focus on the guilty parties: governments and corporate actors.
teachingTranscript.korean: 강조 구문(cleft construction)에 주목하세요: 'it is [X] that are to blame.' 유책 당사자인 정부들과 기업 행위자들에게 모든 초점을 정면으로 집중시킵니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Observe the author's moral language: 'cold and cynical attitude.' This is not neutral reporting; it is a sharp, reasoned ethical indictment.
teachingTranscript.korean: 작가의 도덕적 언어에 주목하세요: 'cold and cynical attitude(냉혹하고 냉소적인 태도).' 이것은 중립적 전달을 넘어 날카롭고 이성적인 윤리적 고발입니다.
